questions.prompt: What are the two kinds of electric charge?
questions.explanation: Charge is positive (protons) or negative (electrons); those are the only two kinds.
questions.misconception: Everyday pairings like left/right or heavy/light are not charges at all.

questions.prompt: A positive ball and a negative ball are placed near each other. What happens?
questions.explanation: Opposite signs attract — this is the golden rule of charge.
questions.misconception: Many flip the rule; like signs repel, opposite signs attract.

questions.prompt: Two balloons both rub on wool and both become negative. When brought close, they...
questions.explanation: Like signs repel — two negative balloons push each other apart.
questions.misconception: The 'opposites only attract' memory is incomplete; like charges repel is its twin.

questions.prompt: When you rub a balloon on your hair, what actually moves from the hair to the balloon?
questions.explanation: Electrons are the light negative particles that rub off and onto objects; protons stay put.
questions.misconception: Imagining protons or whole hair bundles moving; only electrons travel in rubbing.

questions.prompt: When the spark leaps across the bench and the arrows drop to zero, what has happened?
options: Charge found a path and balanced
questions.explanation: Charge is conserved — it flows along the spark path until the imbalance cancels, leaving zero force.
questions.misconception: The 'charge vanishes' belief; it only redistributes along a path.
